canonical_statement: DAPA-HF evaluated whether dapagliflozin, added to recommended therapy, reduces worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death in patients with chronic heart failure and reduced ejection fraction.

canonical_statement: DAPA-HF was a phase 3, international, multicenter, event-driven, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
The trial randomized 4,744 participants at 410 centers in 20 countries.
Participants assigned to active treatment received dapagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily in addition to recommended heart-failure therapy.

exposures.details: Randomized double-blind study treatment added to background heart-failure therapy.

canonical_statement: The control group received matching placebo once daily in addition to recommended heart-failure therapy.

exposures.details: Randomized matching placebo added to background heart-failure therapy.

canonical_statement: Randomization used an approximately 1:1 allocation ratio.
Primary and secondary efficacy analyses included all randomized participants according to the intention-to-treat principle.
The primary analysis used a closed testing procedure with prespecified hierarchical testing and a two-sided alpha of 0.0499 accounting for one interim efficacy analysis.
The safety population included randomized participants who received at least one dose of dapagliflozin or placebo.

population.label: DAPA-HF safety population who received at least one study dose

canonical_statement: The source packet includes the original protocol dated 26 October 2016 (version 1.0) and the final protocol dated 26 October 2017 (version 2.0).
The source packet includes the original statistical analysis plan dated 31 January 2017 (version 1.0) and the final statistical analysis plan dated 23 July 2019 (version 3.0).

The protocol specified an international, multicenter, parallel-group, event-driven, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 design comparing dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily with placebo on top of regional standard care.
The protocol planned approximately 4,500 randomized participants after enrollment of approximately 7,000 screened patients across 500 to 600 sites in 20 to 25 countries.
Eligible participants were adults at least 18 years of age with chronic heart failure and left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% or less.
Participants were required to have NYHA functional class II, III, or IV symptoms.

NT-proBNP eligibility generally required at least 600 pg/mL, with lower threshold 400 pg/mL after a recent heart-failure hospitalization and higher threshold 900 pg/mL for atrial fibrillation or flutter.

Key exclusions included recent SGLT2-inhibitor treatment or intolerance, type 1 diabetes, symptomatic hypotension or systolic blood pressure below 95 mm Hg, and eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² or rapidly declining renal function.

canonical_statement: At baseline, 1,983 of 4,744 randomized participants (41.8%) had a history of type 2 diabetes; an additional approximately 3% received a new diabetes diagnosis at screening.
Mean age was 66.2 years in the dapagliflozin group and 66.5 years in placebo.
Women comprised approximately 24% of each randomized group.
Mean left ventricular ejection fraction was approximately 31% in each randomized group.
Median NT-proBNP was 1,428 pg/mL with dapagliflozin and 1,446 pg/mL with placebo.
Baseline eGFR was below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² in 40.6% of dapagliflozin participants and 40.7% of placebo participants.
Baseline sacubitril-valsartan use was 10.5% in the dapagliflozin group and 10.9% in placebo.
Beta-blocker use at baseline was approximately 96% in each group.
Mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonist use at baseline was 71.5% with dapagliflozin and 70.6% with placebo.
Diuretic use at baseline was 93.4% with dapagliflozin and 93.5% with placebo.
The primary outcome was worsening heart failure (hospitalization or urgent visit requiring intravenous therapy) or cardiovascular death.

Supplementary Figure S1 depicts the DAPA-HF trial design and participant flow framework.
Supplementary Figure S2 summarizes the effects of dapagliflozin on worsening heart failure and mortality, complementing the main recurrent-event analysis.
Supplementary Table S1 reports adverse events of interest and serious adverse events, providing expanded safety detail beyond the selected safety outcomes in the main article.
The authors concluded that, among patients with HFrEF, dapagliflozin reduced worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death regardless of the presence or absence of diabetes.
The authors interpreted the benefit as occurring on top of a high background use of guideline-recommended heart-failure therapies.
Restrictive inclusion and exclusion criteria may limit generalizability beyond the enrolled HFrEF population.
Black participants constituted less than 5% of the trial population.
Few very elderly patients with multiple coexisting illnesses were enrolled.
Baseline use of sacubitril-valsartan was low, limiting precision for concurrent ARNI therapy.
The apparent smaller primary-outcome effect in NYHA class III-IV than class II was not mirrored consistently across other severity markers, and the authors cautioned against overinterpreting it.
DAPA-HF was funded by AstraZeneca.

The sponsor and executive committee designed and oversaw the trial; sponsor analyses were independently replicated by an academic group at the University of Glasgow, and the authors stated responsibility for data fidelity and protocol adherence.
